[quote=united_hydronia;60500613][b]March 19th 2026[/b]

A vote of no confidence has been called against the current government, ruled by the Conservative Party, by the social unity party, currently the largest opposition. SUP chairman, Hakan Bozkhan, highlighted several reasons for this vote in his speech to the house of ministers.

A key reason for this was the lack of information released regarding the Sikirskian arctic disturbances. Hakan stated that this signalled corruption on both Hydronias part and Sikirsks part, also stating that the government was allowing Sikirsk to cover up its troubled past by neglecting to release information.

Another, more minor reason was the current deal with the Neue Republik, as part of the THEP-EDU peace deal. It was stated that this deal was unfair on Hydronia and gave the Republik an economic grip on a once independent nation. Hakan has said that the current deal also signals the current governments neglect towards THEP, saying that the alliance is falling into disrepair as of late.

On the topic of THEP, it has also been mentioned that the current government is stalling talks in THEP to create a unified passport system to further the tourism industry. The Conservative Party has frequently stated that it would be money not well spent, diverting said money to oil infrastructure and mining site, which has had the effect of allowing Republik companies to make more money out of Hydronia. This has, like the Sikirskian arctic investigation, also been kept behind closed doors.

When the vote of no confidence was called by the SUP, both the green future party and the liberal party backed the motion, with only the current government and the preservationists not backing the vote. This resulted in a majority, legally empowering the government to hold a reelection, irrespective of their backing of the vote. The next day, President Ahmet Seliban would begrudgingly announce a reelection to be held next week.

[b]The Ponies and the Chaos May 2026[/b]

Communism, it was a word that wasnt unknown to the equines of Equestria, however, it certainly wasnt a word which was too well received, at least not in its purest form. It had once tried to come into Equestria, and had nearly succeeded in overturning the government, however, it failed thanks to pressure from the government of Thýven in the early 30s. However, the word popped up once again, and it had popped up in the place of Sanguivallis, a large state on the white strait, and then it popped up in Astanir. However, there would be no large condemnation from the Equestrian government, nor would they mention it beyond hushed whispers within the Bureau of Investigations, whose eyes as of recent had been turned towards the constitutional crisis in Thýven. 

The Constitutional Crisis of Thýven was an odd occurrence in that particular region of the world, Thýven rarely had crises, but it had now presented itself as an unstable state, unable to hold together even the most basic of unions. With the collapse of Elesyr-Vespurias and the presence of communism, Equestria sat in limbo, caught almost between two worlds. However, to the opportunistic diarchate of the crown of Equestria, the matter held great importance, a chance to perhaps move away from the heavy handed grasp of Thýven and into a more self-deterministic realm. The cards were now in Equestrias hand, so what would they do?
